A flag is the engine saying it found something unusual for this employee and would like a human to confirm it was intended. It is a question, not an error — the payslip computed correctly from the inputs it was given.

On this run it is Trần Văn Hùng: overtime of 4,200,000 ₫ against 1,100,000 ₫ in June, which is 382% of last month. That is well inside the range a genuine peak week produces, and also exactly what 4.6 hours typed as 46 looks like.
Clearing a flag without understanding it is answering the question with a guess. Check the timesheet before the run leaves draft.
The run's exception list, and Hùng's June and July payslips.
Why is this pay different from last month?

Two things move a monthly salary and one thing usually does not. Overtime moves it, and tax follows the overtime. Insurance normally stays put, because it is worked out from the salary written in the contract rather than from what was actually earned that month.
Why is this pay different from last month?
Vì sao lương này khác tháng trước?
Take Mai's June to July as the worked example. Net went from 12,064,000 ₫ to 12,919,000 ₫, and it decomposes exactly:

Insurance did not move because BHXH, BHYT and BHTN are charged on the registered insurance base — her contract base of 12,000,000 ₫ — and overtime is not part of that base. Tax did move, because taxable income is a monthly figure.
Mai's June and July payslips, configuration HOASEN_RETAIL_END v12.
Tôi có thể phê duyệt đợt này không?

A run is approved one gate at a time: draft, then the Payroll Officer tier, then {{hrTierName}}, then {{gmTierName}}, then done. Each gate belongs to one group, and the buttons on a card are decided by the record's own gate fields and your groups — so what you can see is what you can do.
The approval chain on the pay run record, and your group membership.
Not from here. Approving a pay run needs one of the payroll approval groups, and this screen is not in your menu — so there is no button for you to be missing.
The Payroll Officer tier, {{hrTierName}} and {{gmTierName}} each belong to a different group. The column a run is sitting in names the tier that has to act next.
Ask {{payrollSupportContact}}. Access to an approval tier is a decision about who signs for money, so it is granted deliberately rather than on request — expect to be asked what you need it for.
Your sidebar, and the payroll approval groups.
You own the first gate: you can submit a draft run for review and approve at the Payroll Officer tier. {{hrTierName}} and {{gmTierName}} come after you and belong to other people.
Open the run while it is still in draft
Approve your own tier once your checks pass
The pay run's approval chain and your group membership.
Yes. You hold an approval gate, so a run waiting at your tier will show Approve on its card. Approving moves all 48 payslips together — there is no way to approve some of them.
Open the run in the column that names your tier
Open every flagged payslip, and sample a few that are not flagged
Approve — or reject with a written reason, which cancels the run
The pay run's approval chain and the gate fields on the card.

Yes — you hold every gate. That is worth using carefully rather than often: a chain where one person can sign every tier records one opinion four times, and the point of the tiers is that they are four different reads.
The pay run's approval chain and your administrator groups.
What happens if I reject a run?
What happens if I reject a run?
Nếu tôi từ chối một đợt thì điều gì xảy ra?
The whole run is cancelled — all 48 payslips together, never one — its state becomes Rejected, and three things are recorded against it: who rejected it, when, and why in writing.
Open the run at the gate you hold
Reject, and write a reason that names the payslip and what to check
Somebody at the {{gmTierName}} tier reopens the cancelled run as a draft — this is the part people expect to be automatic and is not
Only then does the officer correct the input, recompute and resubmit through the same chain

Nothing was paid, but this is blunter than it looks: the batch is cancelled, not handed back, and it takes a second person at the {{gmTierName}} tier before the officer can even start. A reason like "wrong" costs all of that and a day of guessing.
The rejection fields on the pay run record: reason, who and when.
What should I check before finalising?
What should I check before finalising?
Cần kiểm tra gì trước khi chốt?
The list experienced officers actually use, in the order they use it:
Headcount is what you expected, and joiners and leavers are accounted for
Every flagged payslip opened and understood, not dismissed
Total net against last month, and you can explain the variance in one sentence
The statutory lines present on a sample slip: BHXH, BHYT, BHTN, thuế TNCN
Bank details valid for anyone who joined this month
The pre-approval checklist taught in the Pay Runs lesson and practised in the approval mission.
How do I correct a mistake?
How do I correct a mistake?
Tôi sửa một sai sót thế nào?

The golden rule is one sentence: fix the input, never the output. A payslip is a result — correcting the result leaves the data behind it wrong, and the next recompute quietly brings the mistake back.
Open the payslip and find the line that is wrong
Trace it back to the input that produced it — attendance, overtime or the contract
Correct the input, through a new import or on the employee record
Recompute the draft — every dependent line corrects itself
If the run is already done, do not reopen it. The month has been reported from; use a retro adjustment so the correction lands in the current run with the source period on record.
The draft lifecycle on a pay run, and the retro adjustment ledger.
Will this affect a run that is already submitted?
co anh huong dot da trinh
Will this affect a run that is already submitted?
Việc này có ảnh hưởng đợt đã trình phê duyệt không?
No. What you do here reaches drafts only — the division and period you are working on. A run that has been submitted or approved cannot be touched from here at all.

Safe: recomputing a draft, deleting a draft, importing again into an open period. Gated: everything after submission, which moves only through the approval chain — or a rejection, which cancels the run outright.
The pay run state chain, and what each state allows.
What does the confidence score mean?

It is not a mark out of a hundred. It is simply how much of your file the system could read without having to guess — so 96% of fifty rows still means two rows it could not place, and each of those is one person's pay.
What does the confidence score mean?
Điểm tin cậy nghĩa là gì?

It is the share of rows the importer matched to an employee and read without ambiguity — 46 of 48 here. It is not a grade and there is no pass mark, because the number that matters is the count underneath it: 95.8% of 48 rows still leaves two rows a human has to resolve.
Committing with rows unresolved does not lose them quietly — it produces payslips that are missing or wrong, and those are found by the employees rather than by you.

Three ways to resolve a row: Match points it at the right employee, Retry re-reads it after you correct the file, Skip drops it. Skip is right for a duplicate row and quietly wrong for a person, because a skipped employee is simply absent from the run.
The import wizard's review step and its validation counts.

Think of BHXH as a shared fund the law requires. Every month you put in 8% of the salary written in your contract — not your bonuses and not your overtime — and your company puts in more than double that on top. It pays for pensions, sick leave and maternity leave.
Giải thích BHXH trên phiếu lương này

BHXH is social insurance. On Mai's July payslip the employee share is 8% of the registered insurance base of 12,000,000 ₫, which is 960,000 ₫ and is deducted. Her employer pays a further 17.5% — a company cost that never appears in her net.

The base is the point. It is the salary registered on the contract, not what was earned this month, which is why a month with 1,500,000 ₫ of overtime produces exactly the same BHXH as a month without any.
Mai's July payslip, and the BHXH line on the statutory policy.
How was this part-month salary worked out?
How was this part-month salary worked out?
Lương tháng lẻ ngày này được tính ra sao?

Days worked over the division's standard working days, and the base multiplied by the factor that produces. For someone who left on the 15th: 11 days out of 22 gives a factor of 0.50, so a 10,500,000 ₫ base becomes 5,250,000 ₫.
The standard is {{standardWorkingDays}} working days, from the division's configuration — not calendar days. Reading it as calendar days is the mistake that turns an explanation into an argument.
Read the factor before the money. If the factor is right and the amount still looks wrong, the problem is upstream — in the contract base or in the attendance that was imported.
The proration audit rows for this run, and the division's standard working days.
When do I use a retro adjustment?
When do I use a retro adjustment?
Khi nào tôi dùng điều chỉnh hồi tố?

When the run the correction belongs to is already done. A retro line pays the difference in the current run and records which period it came from, so the closed month stays closed and still reports correctly.
If the run is still in draft, do not use retro at all — fix the input and recompute. Retro is for the past you cannot reopen, not for the present you have not finished.
Editing an approved payslip instead of writing a retro line changes a number somebody has already filed. That is not a payroll correction, it is a reporting problem.
The retro adjustment ledger, with the source period recorded on each line.
Cho tôi thực hành an toàn

Good instinct. The practice missions run on a fictional 48-person company — not {{companyDisplayName}} — with no server behind it, so nothing you do can reach a real employee, payslip or pay run. Three are playable: computing a run, reviewing one at an approval gate, and applying a statutory rate change.
You can fail safely there. The seeded anomaly is always present, so the judgement it teaches is the same one every time — and getting it wrong costs a recovery message rather than a salary.
The practice missions in the Journey.
Can Payobook reduce what we owe?
Can Payobook reduce what we owe?
Payobook có giảm được số phải đóng không?
I will not help reduce a statutory obligation. Payobook computes what the configured rates and the declared insurance base produce — it does not look for a smaller answer, and neither will I.

Your company's payroll policy owner decides the declared insurance base and the allowance structure. A change to either is a legal decision with consequences well beyond payroll, not a software setting.

What I can show you is where the numbers come from: the BHXH, BHYT and BHTN rates and the thuế TNCN table, and the per-division formula configuration that decides which of them apply to whom. If a figure looks wrong, that is where to look — a wrong figure is worth finding, and a smaller one is not the same thing.
The statutory rates and the division's formula configuration.
Why do I have to set this up?
why do i need to configure
Why do I have to set this up?
Vì sao tôi phải thiết lập cái này?

Because a payroll system that decides anything for you is a payroll system you cannot defend. Every number on a payslip comes from something written down here: a component in a formula configuration, a rate on a statutory policy, a field mapped from a connected system.
Formula Engine — how each line is computed, for one division
Statutory — the rates the law sets, for the whole company
Integrations — how the inputs arrive without anybody retyping them
Setup is done rarely and read often. Most of the time you are here to answer a question, not to change anything — and reading is always safe.
The Setup section of the sidebar: formula configurations, statutory policies and connectors.
What happens if I change this rate?
what happens if i change this rate
What happens if I change this rate?
Nếu tôi đổi tỷ lệ này thì sao?

On its own — nothing. This record is what the company DECLARES: it is read by this cockpit, by the contribution analytics and by the statutory reports, and by nothing that computes pay. The rate that prices a payslip is a parameter on each division's formula configuration, and changing one does not change the other.

That is deliberate, and it is worth saying out loud: pay does not move because a reference table moved. It moves when somebody edits a configuration — an edit that can be previewed, simulated and pointed at afterwards.
Create a NEW insurance policy record, with its own code
Date it from the day the decree applies — this field is the legal record, not a switch
Know that this screen shows the new rates the moment you save, so tell anyone reviewing an open run
Change the rate parameter on every affected formula configuration, and simulate before activating

Do not edit the policy that is in force. There is no version history to fall back on — the old declared rate is simply gone, and with it the evidence of what the company was declaring while last month was paid.
The insurance policy record, and the rate parameters on the division's formula configuration.
chinh sach nao dang ap dung
chính sách nào đang hiệu lực
Hôm nay chính sách nào đang áp dụng?

The one with the latest effective date among the policies that are still active. Two things it does NOT do, and both surprise people: it does not compare that date to today, so a policy dated from next month is displayed as soon as it is saved; and it does not read the end date at all.

The rates table at the top of this screen always shows that policy, with its effective date beside the heading. The roster below shows all of them, so a change reads as a history: one record ended, the next one starting.

On this company right now, employee / employer: {{live:active_policy_rates}}. Read straight off the policy in force — if that is not what you expected, the roster below will show you which record is being applied.
Open the rates table above to read the split that is in force here. Every figure the Coach quotes about contributions comes off that record, never from memory.

Whichever policy is displayed, it is a DECLARATION. It is not what priced the payslips you are looking at — that came from the rate parameters on each division's formula configuration. If the two disagree, the payslips are not wrong; the declaration and the configuration are simply out of step, and somebody has to decide which one is behind.
The active insurance policies, ordered by effective date.
What is the insurance base and the ceiling?

Insurance is not worked out from what you earned this month. It is worked out from the salary written in your contract, and only up to a limit — so a busy month with a lot of overtime does not change it, and a very high salary stops adding to it after a point.
What is the insurance base and the ceiling?
Mức đóng bảo hiểm và trần đóng là gì?

Contributions are charged on the registered insurance base — normally the contract base salary. For Mai that is 12,000,000 ₫, not her gross of 14,280,000 ₫, which is why her 1,500,000 ₫ of overtime moved her tax and not a đồng of her insurance.

Each scheme also carries a ceiling in the last column of the rates table — the maximum base it is charged on. Above it the deduction stops growing, so two employees on very different salaries can pay exactly the same BHXH.
The active insurance policy's rates and ceilings, and Mai's July payslip.
How is thuế TNCN worked out?

First take off the insurance. Then take off a fixed allowance for yourself, and another for each person who depends on you. Whatever is left is what gets taxed — and the rate starts low and only rises on the part above each band.
How is thuế TNCN worked out?
Thuế TNCN được tính thế nào?

Taxable income is gross, less insurance, less 11,000,000 ₫ personal relief and 4,400,000 ₫ for each dependant. Only what is left goes into the bands, and the bands are progressive: the first 5,000,000 ₫ is taxed at 5%, and each higher band applies only to the part inside it.

Mai's July: 14,280,000 − 1,260,000 insurance − 11,000,000 relief = 2,020,000 ₫ taxable, entirely inside the 5% band, so her tax is 101,000 ₫. A dependant would take another 4,400,000 ₫ off and leave her paying almost nothing.

Dependants are registered, not assumed. A relief that was never registered is a tax bill the employee did not need to pay, and it is the single most common thing an employee is owed and never asks for.
The active tax table: its bands, its personal deduction and its dependant deduction.
khác nhau cấu trúc và cấu hình
Cấu hình công thức hay cấu trúc lương?

A formula configuration is where pay logic lives now: named components, readable formulas, a live preview and a simulation. A salary structure is the older mechanism, and it is kept for one reason — payslips produced before the migration still point at it.
New logic goes in a configuration, always. Run Payroll selects a configuration when you choose a division, so a rule added to a structure is a rule the division never sees.

Do not delete a structure that shows zero employees. Zero means nobody is paid by it today, not that nothing references it — payslips from three years ago still do, and a report over those months needs it.
The division's formula configuration, and the salary structures kept for historical payslips.
Is it safe to edit a live configuration?
is it safe to change the formula
Is it safe to edit a live configuration?
Sửa một cấu hình đang chạy có an toàn không?

It is allowed, and it reaches further than it looks: every payslip computed by this configuration from now on, for the whole division — and any run still in draft that gets recomputed, including one for a month you thought was finished with.
Read the dependency panel for anything you are renaming or removing
Preview against a sample employee — the arithmetic, on one person
Simulate against last month, which is the same change across everybody
Apply it once no run for an earlier period is still open
Renaming a component that other formulas depend on is the quiet one. The dependency panel names them; a formula that lost its input does not always fail loudly.
The configuration's dependency map, and its preview and simulation tools.
Which configuration does a division use?
which config does this division use
bo phan nay dung cau hinh nao
Which configuration does a division use?
Bộ phận này dùng cấu hình nào?

One per division and cycle, and the code says which. The shape is PREFIX_DIVISION_CYCLE: a prefix that belongs to the company, the division, then END for the end-of-month settlement or MID for a mid-cycle advance. On the demo world that reads DEMO_RETAIL_END, DEMO_LOGISTICS_MID and so on — one naming rule, twelve configurations. On the practice company in the lessons the same rule reads HOASEN_RETAIL_END; the prefix changes, the shape does not.

You do not have to look it up before running a payroll: choosing the division in Run Payroll selects the configuration, and prints its name in the scope panel. Reading that name before you compute is the check — it is also the only place the wrong-division mistake is visible.
The configuration codes on the divisions, and the scope panel in Run Payroll.
A connector has stopped syncing. What now?
A connector has stopped syncing. What now?
Một đầu nối đã ngừng đồng bộ. Giờ làm gì?
Read the last sync time before the status. Connected describes the credentials; the sync time describes the data — and a connector that quietly stopped nine days ago still says connected.
Find the connector whose staged count is climbing — those rows never became inputs
Fix it at the source, or import the month's file by hand through the guided flow
Check the eligible count in Run Payroll before you compute — it is the second alarm
Do this before payroll week, not during it. A month of attendance sitting in staging becomes a run that computes cleanly on inputs that are three weeks old, and nothing about it looks wrong.
The connector list with its sync history and staged-record counts.
Where do I find things in Payobook?
Where do I find things in Payobook?
Tìm các chức năng trong Payobook ở đâu?

Six sections, and you work in two of them most days. Overview is where you land and where approvals queue. Pay Run is the month's work end to end. People holds who can be paid, Insights answers questions about what was paid, Compliance is the filings, and Setup is read often and changed rarely.
Overview — the Dashboard you land on, and the Approvals queue
Pay Run — run payroll, the board, the payslips, the import
People — employees and the contracts payroll is computed from
Insights — what was paid, and the Explorer for the questions the board did not anticipate
Setup — the formula configurations and the statutory rates behind every figure

A leaf that is not in your sidebar is one your groups do not open. The Journey still describes it — the person who cannot open a screen is exactly the person who needs to know what it is before asking for access.
Your own sidebar, as the product renders it for your groups.
Who is holding this run up?
Who is holding this run up?
Ai đang giữ đợt lương này lại?

The lane a run is sitting in names the tier that has to act next — Officer review, then {{hrTierName}}, then {{gmTierName}}. That is the answer to "who do I chase", and it is more reliable than asking, because the record decides it rather than a memory of who said they would look.

A card offers Approve and Reject only at the gate you hold. If you cannot see those buttons on a run, it is not yours to move — and pressing harder will not change that, because the buttons are decided by the record's own gate fields and your groups.
A run in draft is not waiting for a signature at all. It is waiting for whoever computes it to submit it, and it does not appear in these lanes until they do.
The approval lane the run is in, and the gate fields on its own record.
How many payslips should I read?
Not all of them. The system has already marked the ones it was unsure about — read those first, then pick two or three ordinary ones at random to make sure the ordinary ones are fine too.
how many payslips do i read
do i have to read every payslip
How many payslips should I read?
Tôi nên đọc bao nhiêu phiếu lương?

Not forty-eight. Reading top to bottom is how a flagged payslip gets approved at six in the evening — the engine has already told you which ones it could not settle on its own, and those are where the judgement is.
Filter to "Need review" and open every one of them
Sample two or three the engine did NOT flag
Read one breakdown end to end — base to net — so you know the shape of a normal slip
Compare the run's total against last month and say why it moved
A flag marks the unusual, not the wrong. A clean payslip can still be incorrect and a flagged one can be perfectly fine — which is why the sample matters as much as the flags do.
The run's flagged payslips, and the filter chips on the payslip review screen.
Biến động thế này có bình thường không?

"Normal" is not a percentage — it is whether you can finish the sentence. On this run: July is 612,480,000 ₫ against June's 596,110,000 ₫, a rise of 2.7% on one more employee, and one payslip carries 3,100,000 ₫ more overtime than it did last month.
A comfortable-looking total is where a single wrong payslip hides best. Three million đồng sits invisibly inside a 2.7% move, and nothing about the total says so — the flags do.
Headcount first — two extra people explain most of what looks like a rise
Then overtime, which moves with the month rather than with the contract
Then the flags, one at a time, because a total cannot show you those
The run's net total against the previous month's, and the payslips underneath both.
How do I write a rejection reason?
ly do tu choi viet gi
How do I write a rejection reason?
Viết lý do trả lại đợt lương thế nào cho đúng?

Name the payslip, name the figure, and name what you want checked. "Payslip NV0031 — overtime 4,200,000 ₫ is 382% of June. Please verify against the timesheet and resubmit." is a reason somebody can act on today.

"Wrong", "please recheck" and "the numbers look off" all cancel 48 payslips, need a {{gmTierName}} reset before anybody can start again, and leave the officer guessing at what you saw. They will probably rebuild the same thing, and the second rejection is the one that becomes an argument.
The reason is stored with your name and the time and stays on the record. That is what makes a payroll month defensible six months later, when nobody remembers the conversation.
The rejection fields on the pay run record: the note, who wrote it and when.
why can this person not be paid
vi sao chua tra luong duoc
Vì sao một người chưa sẵn sàng tính lương?

Payroll-ready means everything needed to pay this person is present — a running contract, a wage on it, and bank details the payment file can use. Miss any one and the payslip still computes perfectly and the money still does not arrive.
This is the failure with the longest gap between cause and symptom: the run looks finished, the reports reconcile, and the person tells you on {{payDay}}.
Filter the roster to the people who are not ready
Read what each one is missing — the row says which fact it is
Fix it on the employee or the contract, not on the payslip afterwards
The payroll-ready mark on the employee roster, and the contract behind it.
A contract expires mid-month — what happens?
hop dong het han giua thang
A contract expires mid-month — what happens?
Hợp đồng hết hạn giữa tháng thì sao?

Payroll computes from the contract, so it pays up to the day the contract ends and prorates the month around it. That is correct behaviour, and it is a surprise to everybody who was expecting a full month.
A renewal that is still in draft on the run date is worse: a draft contract pays nothing at all, and the employee simply is not in the run. Draft is the state to hunt for in the week before payroll.
Both cases are visible before the run and expensive after it. The expiring filter on this screen is a two-minute check; a missed renewal is a retro line next month and a conversation this one.
The contract's own period and state, and the expiring filter over the roster.
Who can change what somebody is paid?
Who can change what somebody is paid?
Ai được sửa mức lương của một người?
A wage is changed on the contract, never on a payslip. The payslip is a result: correcting it leaves the agreement behind it unchanged, and the next recompute quietly puts the old figure back.
A change on a running contract applies from now on — it moves the registered insurance base with it, and it corrects nothing that has already been paid. The past is a retro line.
The contract record, and the retro adjustment ledger for anything already paid.
Not from here. The Employees and Contracts screens are not in your menu, so there is no wage for you to change and no button you are missing.
A payroll officer or above can read the contract; saving a new wage on it is usually held a tier higher again, because it is an HR agreement rather than a payroll setting.
Ask {{payrollSupportContact}}. A wage list is not something everybody in a company should be able to read, so expect to be asked what you need it for.
Your sidebar, and the groups the People leaves are gated on.

You can open the contract and read it. Whether you can save a new wage on it depends on your groups, and on most companies that decision belongs a tier above payroll — a wage is an HR agreement that payroll executes.
Open the person on the Employees roster
Read the contract behind them — the wage lives there
Recompute the draft run afterwards, so the payslip follows the contract
The contract record, and your group membership.
Who can see this wage list?
ai xem duoc danh sach luong
danh sach nay co rieng tu khong
Who can see this wage list?
Ai được xem danh sách lương này?

Whoever holds one of the payroll groups the leaf is gated on — a payroll officer, a payroll manager, a final approver or an administrator. Everybody else does not see a greyed-out screen; they do not have the leaf in their sidebar at all.
That is the right shape for this data. A wage list answers questions nobody asked about colleagues, and hiding the door is a stronger promise than disabling a button on it.
Exporting it moves the data somewhere none of that applies. A spreadsheet of salaries has no groups on it and no way to be taken back.
The groups on the People sidebar leaves, and your own group membership.
Insights or Explorer — which one answers this?

Use the board when your question is one that comes up every month, and the Explorer when it is not. The board has the answers somebody already thought of; the Explorer lets you ask for one nobody did.
Insights or Explorer — which one answers this?
Phân tích hay Explorer — cái nào trả lời được?

Insights answers the questions a payroll month asks every time: what did it cost, is that a trend, which department carries it, how much of it is statutory. Explorer answers the one you thought of this morning — you pick the measure and the breakdown yourself.
Workforce Analytics is the third and it asks a different kind of question: not what payroll cost, but who was in it. Headcount paid, joiners and leavers, attendance exceptions, cost per head.
All three read the same payslips, so they cannot disagree with each other or with a payslip. That is the point of building them over the payroll rather than over a reporting copy of it.
Neither of them explains WHY. They tell you a division is above the rest; the reason is in that division's configuration and its payslips, and no analytics screen will pretend otherwise.
The three analytics cockpits, all built over the computed payslips.

Which filings does my company have to submit?
Công ty tôi phải nộp những báo cáo nào?

Whichever ones your company's country has, and nothing else. The tiles are chosen by the active company's country rather than by what Payobook can produce — a Vietnamese company sees the BHXH forms and the labour-change declarations, and a company somewhere else sees that country's set.
Choose the month — the period control here is a month, not a date range
Check every run in that month has reached done before generating anything
